concepts.title: Glycolysis and Its Net ATP Gain

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Glycolysis and Its Net ATP Gain' refers to.
questions.a: Glycolysis is the partial oxidation of one glucose molecule to two molecules of pyruvic acid through ten enzymatic steps in the cytoplasm, producing a net gain of two ATP and two NADH under anaerobic conditions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Glycolysis and Its Net ATP Gain'.
questions.a: Glycolysis splits hexose into two triose sugars through a prepatory phase using ATP and a payoff phase generating ATP and NADH, and it is common to aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Glycolysis and Its Net ATP Gain' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Fermentation: Anaerobic Fate of Pyruvate' refers to.
questions.a: Under anaerobic conditions pyruvic acid is reduced by NADH to lactic acid in muscles or to ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast, and fermentation yields only a net gain of two ATP per glucose with far less energy released than aerobic respiration.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fermentation: Anaerobic Fate of Pyruvate'.
questions.a: The enzymes pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase carry out alcoholic fermentation in yeast, and lactic acid fermentation happens in muscle cells during exercise.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Fermentation: Anaerobic Fate of Pyruvate' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Amphibolic Pathway and Respiratory Balance Sheet

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Amphibolic Pathway and Respiratory Balance Sheet' refers to.
questions.a: Respiration is an amphibolic pathway because the respiratory intermediates serve both catabolism and anabolism, and the respiratory balance sheet is theoretical since ATP amounts depend on the shuttle of electrons, the mitochondrial state and the pathway taken.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Amphibolic Pathway and Respiratory Balance Sheet'.
questions.a: Acetyl CoA drawn from fats, carbohydrates and proteins enters the same Krebs cycle, proving the amphibolic nature of respiration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Amphibolic Pathway and Respiratory Balance Sheet' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 12.4.4 The Respiratory Balance Sheet, 12.4.5 Amphibolic Pathway (source: kebo112.txt sections 12.4.4, 12.4.5)
